horses.spotlight_comment: Testing Patience is the one they all have to beat but MR FINCH ran well for a long way in a stronger race than this at Newbury. Jorah d'Alma has each-way claims after shaping better in a tongue-tie at Bangor.[Alistair Jones] Page 1 spotlightwarwick 23.04.26

Moon 7 12-0p1 E Lavelle Ben Jones 2-1 130 108 130 Only stepped up to 3m in his last three races and went close in two of those; looked as though he'd win at Newbury last time (good to soft) only to get outbattled; the cheekpieces could be significant. Thank You Ma'Am 7 11-8tb Ms G Nicholls Miss Olive Nicholls (5) 5-1 124 125 130 Back hurdling the last twice after a brief stint over fences; the first time he'd worn these aids combined when a front-running third at Wetherby (3m, good; beaten 4.25l); exposed but firmly in the mix. Step Ahead 6 11-6t K Bailey & M Nicholls Ciaran Gethings 5-2 122 107 129 Second to the smart Moneygarrow here before winning a maiden at Cheltenham (2m4f, good); back on track with a 4l third over 2m5f at Kempton and going further this afternoon could help him on handicap debut; respected. Lipa K 8 11-5p O Greenall & J Guerriero Charlie Todd 4-1 121 127 128 Goes particularly well at Bangor but was runner-up at Aintree on final run in October (3m, good); however, a 3lb rise sees him on a career-high mark and he's been off a good while. Benign Dictator 9 11-4b O Murphy Tom Hutsby (10) 15-2 120 129 132 Career-best form came here in December when scoring over 3m2f (good to soft); hasn't really approached that level since, in cheekpieces and blinkers (new) the last twice. Everyonesgame 9 10-11 Andy Irvine Caoilin Quinn 25-1 113 118 127 Below par last time at Ascot but Kempton win in November was off only 4lb lower and then ran fairly well at Cheltenham; if back to that level of form then he wouldn't be far away.

The application of cheekpieces could be key for J J MOON who looked as though he would win at Newbury before outbattled late on. Step Ahead might well improve for this longer trip on his handicap debut and he earns second preference ahead of Thank You Ma'am in what is a trappy handicap.[Alistair Jones] Page 2 spotlightwarwick 23.04.26

This final is usually staged at Cheltenham and was won last April by Minniemum who needs to pull her socks up if she's to make a successful defence. Genuine good ground would be a first for HOLETOWN but it was an excellent run on good to soft at Newbury last time and she's back against her own sex here. Last year's third Kosasiempre has a solid chance, along with Party Vibes and Theonewedreamof.[Alistair Jones] Page 3 spotlightwarwick 23.04.26

Mares' Challenger Series Final Handicap Hurdle (Series Final) (GBB Race) £50,000 Total Race Value RTV 2m5f For 4yo+ fillies & mares which have been placed in the first eight on at least one occasion in a Challenger Mares' Hurdle Series Qualifier during the current season Minimum weight 10-2 Penalties after April 11th, a winner of a hurdle 7lb; NOTE: Any horse rated above 135 shall initially be treated as having that rating and the highest weight allotted shall be 12st. Subsequently, the excess over 135 in any rating shall be allotted to that horse without limitation to the highest weight to be carried Penalty value 1st £26,015 2nd £11,960 3rd £5,980 4th £2,990 5th £1,495 6th £745 GOOD Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR Siog Geal 7 12-0 F O'Brien Fern O'Brien (5) 6-1 127 120 128 Had Pismo Beach in third when winning last season's mares' final at Newbury (2m4f, good); has had another good campaign off her tough mark and went down narrowly last time at Chepstow (2m3f, soft) with Fern O'Brien claiming her 5lb; back up 1lb; each-way claims. Rockola Vogue 7 11-13p D Killahena & G McPherson David Bass 12-1 126 124 129 Picked up two handicaps in the autumn (2m3f/2m7f, good) but her progress has rather stalled since then and looks on a hard mark. Rula Bula 7 11-8 J & A J O'Neill Jonjo O'Neill Jr 20-1 121 113 129 Last season started well but petered out and it might be happening again, as although it wasn't a bad run behind Cheltenham Festival heroine White Noise two starts back, Chepstow last time was underwhelming (well behind Siog Geal; soft ground no excuse). Greyval 7 11-5p1 F O'Brien Jonathan Burke 12-1 118 114 131 Won this race last year (at Cheltenham) off today's mark; turned her back on chasing this winter and ran quite well over 3m at Kempton before finding soft ground too testing at Ludlow; plenty looks in her favour this time with cheekpieces added. Pretending 7 11-4p Mrs L Wadham Tom Cannon 6-1 117 116 131 Third to Greyval 12 months ago off the same mark; hadn't been at her best this season but came good at Market Rasen (2m4f, soft) and clearly capable of having some say in the outcome. Service Minimum 6 11-3 D Skelton Harry Skelton 7-2 116 116 122 Would have found conditions too soft when seventh behind Pretending at Market Rasen and she then justified market confidence with a narrow win at Bangor (2m3f, good); she travelled much the best in that race but the handicapper went with an 11lb rise and that asks major questions in this loftier grade. Crazierthandaisy 7 11-2 N Henderson Nico de Boinville 6-1 115 126 128 Looked a bit unlucky not to win at Uttoxeter last time (2m4f, good to soft) but wouldn't be certain to run as well again given her inconsistency; 5lb above the only mark she's defied in a handicap and a 7lb claimer was employed last time. Hard Dealt 6 11-1 H Daly Sam Twiston-Davies 13-2 114 119 127 Has only won a Worcester novice and failed in six handicaps off lower marks, though was runner-up in four of those; clearly has nothing up her sleeve mark-wise but should still run well. Pismo Beach 6 11-1t S Edmunds Charlie Hammond 9-2 114 124 129 Placed for a second time in last month's Grade 2 mares' novices handicap at Newbury (good to soft), this season beating all bar the talented Charisma Cat who went on to run well in a Grade 1 at Aintree; bumped up 4lb for that but this mare will enjoy the good ground; chance. Audacious Annie 7 10-12p J Snowden Gavin Sheehan 12-1 111 127 129 First and second in her two previous visits here, latterly over this far in first-time cheekpieces in November; below best in her last two races (3m/2m4f) and appears to have little margin for error off this mark; absent since January. Keep On Cobbling 6 10-2 H Daly Harry Bannister 20-1 101 102 122 Maiden winner who made a successful handicap debut at Sedgefield (2m5f, good) but hasn't advanced her form from there; however, soft ground perhaps not ideal the last time and this 6yo is bred to improve with her racing. Country Mouse 6 10-2p1 A Ralph Liam Harrison 40-1 101 113 127 Point winner; the Ludlow third in December (2m5f novice; good to soft) offers some hope off this mark but lesser runs have followed, including her handicap debut when a 25-1 chance; cheekpieces added.

It's a different day and a different track but GREYVAL (nap) won last year's final of this and she has plenty in her favour for a bold defence. Stablemate Siog Geal is feared most on the back of what has been a very solid campaign. Pismo Beach is another strong contender after her excellent run at Newbury.[Alistair Jones] Page 4 spotlightwarwick 23.04.26

After from a break, back on better ground and with headgear removed, ZOEMAN can be given another chance. Forcetoreckonwith has to be feared with the form of her last win franked and it wouldn't be a surprise should Ironica De Thaix turn a corner.[Alistair Jones] Page 5 spotlightwarwick 23.04.26

The handicapper has dug his claws in with a 10lb rise for INION TIOGAIR's latest win at Chepstow but she found new reserves for an impressive win and may be up to the task. Topweight Killycarn can be the main danger after his stout effort in a higher grade at Musselburgh, while Orange Diamond, Can't Resist It and Snapius are others to consider.[Emily Weber] Page 6 spotlightwarwick 23.04.26

This looks open. The suggestion is SLEEPING SATELLITE who ran well in a higher grade last time and he's in first-time cheekpieces. Second choice Claim Du Brizais might be getting to grips with fences after a better run here month. Two To Tango is preferred of the others.[Alistair Jones] Page 7 spotlightwarwick 23.04.26

121) and Some Front (point); dam unraced half-sister to 2m6f-3m hurdle/chase winner Off The Charts; one of two debutants for stable enjoying a productive season in bumpers; watch the betting. Olly's Icon 4 10-9 Mrs C Williams Ellis Collier (5) 33-1 - - - Fourth foal; dam unraced half-sister to two winners (hurdle/Flat), out of 1m4f winner; others newcomers make greater appeal on paper. The Drunken Sailor 4 10-9 C Gordon Tom Cannon 10-1 - - - Fourth foal; dam unplaced in bumper and 2m3f-3m1f hurdles, half-sister to bumper and useful 2m1f-2m2f hurdle/chase winner Watcombe Heights, out of bumper and 2m5f/2m6f hurdle winner; trainer does well in bumpers and he could go well on debut.

The mare FOR A MOMENT returns from a break with her trainer Fergal O'Brien firmly among the winners and the form of her bumper debut second at Ludlow two starts ago has worked out very well. She earns the vote ahead of two-time runner-up Lion Rose Sivola, with Wincanton winner Nevada Samba third choice. Lightsoutandaway and Norff N Sauff are interesting newcomers for Gary and Josh Moore, likewise The Drunken Sailer for Chris Gordon.[Ben Hutton] Page 9
